- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.2) and forecast is trending down, avoid overcorrecting; maintain slight upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show strong mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive downward moves), model should not overreact to recent spikes.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– 0.2–0.4), model should smooth transitions — avoid abrupt 10–15% swings in forecast unless supported by strong sentiment momentum.  
- If true outcome deviates from forecast by > 3% in the first 5 days of the 30d window, adjust forecast downward if sentiment is weak or upward if sentiment is strong — apply a 1–2 day lag correction.  
- For 30d forecasts, if the last 3–5 values in history are close to the 30d forecast mean, reduce forecast variance — avoid overfitting to recent noise.
